editorial.headline: Textile Garment Manufacturing, From Cut Cloth to Ready-to-Wear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 14111 covers textile-based ready-made clothing production, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record provided.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14111 is the industrial home for making ready-to-wear garments from textile fabric. The record describes a practical manufacturing activity: cloth is cut and sewn until it becomes clothing ready for use. Its examples are broad but still tightly tied to textile konfeksi: shirts, trousers, kebaya, blouses, skirts, baby clothing, dance clothing, nightgowns, dressing gowns, pyjamas, and sportswear. It also includes disposable ready-made garments made from textiles, as well as textile parts of bras, including straps and cups.

The scope is not limited to plain fabric. It also reaches garments made from embroidered cloth and patchwork fabric, which matters because the defining activity is still the textile-garment process: turning woven, knitted, or non-woven fabric into wearable apparel through cutting and sewing. This is manufacturing, not retail branding in disguise. A company registering this activity should be describing an operation that produces finished textile clothing, whether the output is everyday apparel, ceremonial clothing, sportswear, sleepwear, or specific textile components identified in the record.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity can describe anything from a very small konfeksi workshop to a larger garment manufacturing operation, provided the registered business actually matches the production scope. The scale choice is not cosmetic: it should follow the real size and operating profile of the business. But the record itself does not narrow this KBLI to one business size. It places the activity across the full scale ladder named in the data.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For Bali, the same record does not create a separate foreign-ownership percentage, cap, quota, or partnership condition. It marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest reading is straightforward: nationally open, up to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.
